## Introduction

Compositional diet data — where each observation is a vector of prey proportions summing to one — is challenging to model because most entries are structural zeros (prey not observed in that stomach). Two different statistical approaches are compared here:

**zoid** (Zero-and-One Inflated Dirichlet; Anderson & Ward 2022) handles zeros through per-category zero-inflation parameters fitted separately for each prey item.

**Ordered Dirichlet (Single Shared Mean)** is a custom Stan model where a single global threshold τ governs sparsity across *all* categories simultaneously. Activity for category *k* is driven by `sigmoid(θ_k − τ)`, where `θ = β'X` is a category-specific linear predictor and `softmax(θ)` is the Dirichlet mean direction. This couples mean direction and sparsity through the same parameters, with τ as the only global sparsity knob.

**ZADR (Zero-Adjusted Dirichlet Regression; Tsagris & Stewart 2018)** handles zeros by treating each distinct zero pattern as a latent group. The probability of each group is estimated empirically (θ_b = n_b / N), and within each group the non-zero components follow a Dirichlet whose mean is the renormalized softmax of the covariate-linked linear predictor, with a shared precision φ.

**Coupled Ordered Dirichlet** extends the Ordered Dirichlet by (1) allowing all-zero rows naturally — the empty active set $A_i = \varnothing$ corresponds to an all-zero row, so no truncation denominator is needed — and (2) adding an inclusion-scale parameter $a_\rho > 0$ that modulates how sharply the latent score $\theta_{ik}$ drives component activity. Each component is included via $z_{ik} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(\sigma(a_\rho\theta_{ik}-\tau))$ independently.

All four models are fit to the `coddiet` dataset with intercept-only and Season-covariate specifications and compared via leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO-IC).

```{r}

#| cache: false
library(zoid)
library(cmdstanr)
library(posterior)
library(loo)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)

set.seed(123)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Model Specifications

### Shared Notation

Let $\mathbf{y}_i = (y_{i1}, \ldots, y_{iK})^\top \in \mathcal{S}^K$ be a $K$-dimensional compositional observation for subject $i = 1, \ldots, N$, where $y_{ik} \geq 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^K y_{ik} = 1$. Let $\mathbf{X}$ be the $N \times P$ design matrix with rows $\mathbf{x}_i^\top$.

The softmax mean vector is $$\boldsymbol{\mu}_i = \operatorname{softmax}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_i), \qquad
  \boldsymbol{\theta}_i = \boldsymbol{\beta}^\top \mathbf{x}_i \in \mathbb{R}^K,$$ with one reference category constrained to zero. Define the *active set* for observation $i$ as $A_i = \{k : y_{ik} > 0\}$, and the renormalized active mean $$\tilde{\mu}_{ik} = \frac{\mu_{ik}}{\sum_{k' \in A_i} \mu_{ik'}}, \quad k \in A_i.$$

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Model 1: zoid

zoid (Anderson & Ward 2022) assigns an independent per-category zero-inflation probability $\pi_k$ and links the Dirichlet mean to covariates via softmax. Letting $\phi$ be the Dirichlet precision, the marginal density of the $k$-th component for observation $i$ is

$$p(y_{ik}) = \pi_k \cdot \mathbf{1}[y_{ik}=0]
            + (1 - \pi_k) \cdot f_{\mathrm{Beta}}(y_{ik};\, \phi\mu_{ik},\, \phi(1-\mu_{ik})),$$

and the joint log-likelihood is accumulated at the **observation** $\times$ category level (yielding $N \times K$ pointwise values for LOO):

$$\ell^{\mathrm{zoid}} = \sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{k=1}^K
  \log p(y_{ik} \mid \boldsymbol{\mu}_i, \phi, \boldsymbol{\pi}).$$

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Model 2: Ordered Dirichlet (Single Shared Mean)

A single global threshold $\tau$ governs sparsity. The per-category activity probability is $$\rho_{ik} = \sigma(\theta_{ik} - \tau), \quad
  \sigma(x) = (1 + e^{-x})^{-1},$$ and the precision is covariate-linked: $\phi_i = \exp(\boldsymbol{\delta}^\top \mathbf{x}_i)$.

The observation-level log-likelihood conditions on the active set $A_i$ being non-empty:

$$\ell_i^{\mathrm{ord}} =
  \underbrace{
    \sum_{k \in A_i} \log\rho_{ik} + \sum_{k \notin A_i}\log(1-\rho_{ik})
    - \log\!\Bigl(1 - \prod_{k=1}^K(1-\rho_{ik})\Bigr)
  }_{\text{Bernoulli zero pattern, conditioned on }A_i \neq \emptyset}
  + \underbrace{
    \log\mathrm{Dir}\!\bigl(\mathbf{y}_{A_i}\mid\phi_i\,\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{A_i}\bigr)
  }_{\text{Dirichlet over active set (}|A_i|>1\text{)}}.$$

Reference category: $\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\cdot K} = \mathbf{0}$.

**Stan `lpdf`:**

``` stan
real ordered_dirichlet_shared_lpdf(
    vector y, vector theta, real phi, real tau) {
  int K = num_elements(y);
  vector[K] mu  = softmax(theta);
  vector[K] eta = theta - tau;           // activity logits
  int A_size = 0;
  array[K] int active;
  real lp_A = 0; real log_empty = 0;

  for (k in 1:K) {
    real log_rho   = -log1p_exp(-eta[k]);
    real log1m_rho = -log1p_exp( eta[k]);
    log_empty += log1m_rho;
    if (y[k] > 0) { A_size += 1; active[A_size] = k; lp_A += log_rho; }
    else           {                                   lp_A += log1m_rho; }
  }
  lp_A -= log1m_exp(log_empty);         // condition on at least one active

  if (A_size == 1) return lp_A;

  vector[A_size] y_A; vector[A_size] alpha_A; real mu_sum = 0;
  for (a in 1:A_size) mu_sum += mu[active[a]];
  for (a in 1:A_size) {
    y_A[a]     = y[active[a]];
    alpha_A[a] = phi * mu[active[a]] / mu_sum;   // renormalized concentration
  }
  return lp_A + dirichlet_lpdf(y_A | alpha_A);
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Model 3: ZADR

Each distinct zero pattern $\mathbf{g}_{b} \in \{0,1\}^K$ defines a latent group with empirical probability $\theta_b = n_b / N$ (where $n_b$ is the count of observations with that pattern). Given group $b^*(i)$ for observation $i$, the non-zero components follow $\mathbf{y}_{A_i} \sim \mathrm{Dir}(\phi\,\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{A_i})$. Because $\sum_{k \in A_i}\tilde{\mu}_{ik} = 1$, the sum of Dirichlet concentrations is always $\phi$, so $\log\Gamma(\phi)$ is the normalizing constant for every pattern.

The observation-level log-likelihood is (Tsagris & Stewart 2018, Eq. 8):

$$\ell_i^{\mathrm{zadr}} =
  \log\theta_{b^*(i)}
  + \log\Gamma(\phi)
  - \sum_{k \in A_i}\log\Gamma(\phi\,\tilde{\mu}_{ik})
  + \sum_{k \in A_i}(\phi\,\tilde{\mu}_{ik} - 1)\log y_{ik}.$$

Reference category: $\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\cdot 1} = \mathbf{0}$ (component 1 is baseline, following the Compositional R package convention).

---

### Model 3b: Bayesian ZADR

The fixed-theta ZADR treats $\theta_b = n_b/N$ as a plug-in estimate. A fully
Bayesian extension places a symmetric Dirichlet prior on the $B$ pattern
probabilities:

$$\boldsymbol{\theta} \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\alpha_0 \mathbf{1}_B),$$

where $\alpha_0 = 1$ gives a uniform prior over the simplex. The log-likelihood
for observation $i$ is identical to Eq.\ (ZADR) above, with $\theta_{b^*(i)}$
now a latent parameter:

$$\ell_i^{\mathrm{zadr\text{-}bayes}} =
  \log\theta_{b^*(i)}
  + \log\Gamma(\phi)
  - \sum_{k \in A_i}\log\Gamma(\phi\,\tilde{\mu}_{ik})
  + \sum_{k \in A_i}(\phi\,\tilde{\mu}_{ik} - 1)\log y_{ik}.$$

The data block passes integer pattern identifiers `pattern_id[i]` ∈ \{1,…,B\}
instead of the precomputed `log_theta`, and estimates `simplex[B] theta`
alongside $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ and $\phi$.

**Stan model block:**
```stan
parameters {
  matrix[P, K - 1] beta_raw;
  real<lower=0>    phi;
  simplex[B]       theta;       // stochastic zero-pattern probabilities
}
model {
  to_vector(beta_raw) ~ normal(0, 1);
  phi   ~ gamma(2, 0.1);
  theta ~ dirichlet(rep_vector(alpha_0, B));
  for (i in 1:N) {
    vector[K] mu = softmax(beta' * to_vector(X[i]'));
    y[i] ~ zadr(mu, phi, log(theta[pattern_id[i]]));
  }
}
```

---

### Model 4: Coupled Ordered Dirichlet

The coupled model replaces the conditioned inclusion of the Ordered Dirichlet with independent Bernoulli draws — no truncation is needed because the empty active set is the all-zero row. An extra scale parameter $a_\rho > 0$ controls how sharply the latent score drives inclusion.

For all-zero rows ($s_i = 0$):
$$\ell_i^{\mathrm{coupled}} = \sum_{k=1}^K \log(1-\rho_{ik}), \qquad \rho_{ik} = \sigma(a_\rho\theta_{ik}-\tau).$$

For nonzero rows ($s_i > 0$), letting $A_i = \{k : y_{ik} > 0\}$:
$$\ell_i^{\mathrm{coupled}} =
  \sum_{k \in A_i}\log\rho_{ik}
  + \sum_{k \notin A_i}\log(1-\rho_{ik})
  + \mathbf{1}(|A_i|\ge 2)\,\log\mathrm{Dir}\!\bigl(\tilde{\mathbf{y}}_{A_i}\mid\phi_i\,\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{A_i}\bigr).$$

Precision is log-linear: $\phi_i = \exp(\boldsymbol{\delta}^\top\mathbf{x}_i)$. Reference category: $\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\cdot K} = \mathbf{0}$.

**Stan `lpdf`:**

``` stan
real coupled_ordered_dirichlet_lpdf(
    vector y, vector theta, real phi, real tau, real a_rho, real eps) {
  int K = num_elements(y);
  real total = sum(y);
  vector[K] mu = softmax(theta);
  real lp_A = 0;

  if (total <= eps) {
    for (k in 1:K)
      lp_A += bernoulli_logit_lpmf(0 | a_rho * theta[k] - tau);
    return lp_A;
  }
  vector[K] y_norm = y / total;
  int A_size = 0; array[K] int active;
  for (k in 1:K) {
    real eta_k = a_rho * theta[k] - tau;
    if (y_norm[k] > eps) { A_size += 1; active[A_size] = k;
                            lp_A += bernoulli_logit_lpmf(1 | eta_k); }
    else                  { lp_A += bernoulli_logit_lpmf(0 | eta_k); }
  }
  if (A_size == 1) return lp_A;
  vector[A_size] y_A; vector[A_size] alpha_A; real mu_sum = 0;
  for (a in 1:A_size) mu_sum += mu[active[a]];
  for (a in 1:A_size) {
    y_A[a]     = y_norm[active[a]];
    alpha_A[a] = phi * mu[active[a]] / mu_sum;
  }
  return lp_A + dirichlet_lpdf(y_A | alpha_A);
}
```

---

**Stan `lpdf` (shared by both ZADR variants):**

``` stan
real zadr_lpdf(vector y, vector mu, real phi, real log_theta) {
  int K = num_elements(y);
  real mu_active_sum = 0;
  real lgamma_sum    = 0;
  real y_terms       = 0;

  for (k in 1:K)
    if (y[k] > 0) mu_active_sum += mu[k];

  for (k in 1:K) {
    if (y[k] > 0) {
      real mu_k    = mu[k] / mu_active_sum;   // renormalize to active set
      real alpha_k = phi * mu_k;
      lgamma_sum  += lgamma(alpha_k);
      y_terms     += (alpha_k - 1) * log(y[k]);
    }
  }
  // lgamma(phi) = lgamma(sum alpha_k) since renormalized mu sums to 1
  return log_theta + lgamma(phi) - lgamma_sum + y_terms;
}
```

## Data

The `coddiet` dataset contains cod stomach samples from the Faroe Bank, stratified by Year and Season. Columns are prey item biomass measurements.

```{r}
#| label: data
data(coddiet)

design_raw <- coddiet[, c("Year", "Season")]
data_raw   <- coddiet[, !names(coddiet) %in% c("Year", "Season")]

design_raw$Season <- as.factor(design_raw$Season)
design_raw$Year   <- as.factor(design_raw$Year)

# Drop rows with zero total biomass (no prey found)
row_totals <- rowSums(data_raw)
keep       <- row_totals > 0
data_raw   <- data_raw[keep, ]
design_raw <- design_raw[keep, ]

# Row-normalise to proportions for the ordered Dirichlet model
Y_prop <- as.matrix(data_raw) / rowSums(data_raw)

# coddiet has K=30 prey categories but only N=10 observations.
# Reduce to the top K_max prey by non-zero frequency so both models are
# tractable and not severely overparameterised.
K_max <- 10L
prey_freq  <- colMeans(Y_prop > 0)
top_prey   <- names(sort(prey_freq, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(K_max)]
data_raw   <- data_raw[, top_prey]
Y_prop     <- Y_prop[, top_prey]
# Some rows may now be all-zero if their prey were outside the top set
keep2      <- rowSums(data_raw) > 0
data_raw   <- data_raw[keep2, ]
design_raw <- design_raw[keep2, ]
Y_prop     <- Y_prop[keep2, ]
Y_prop     <- Y_prop / rowSums(Y_prop)   # re-normalise after column drop

N <- nrow(Y_prop)
K <- ncol(Y_prop)
prey_names <- colnames(Y_prop)

cat(sprintf("N = %d stomachs, K = %d prey categories (top %d by frequency)\n",
            N, K, K_max))
cat(sprintf("Overall zero proportion: %.2f\n", mean(Y_prop == 0)))
cat("\nSeason counts:\n"); print(table(design_raw$Season))

# Precompute log_theta for ZADR: log(proportion of obs sharing the same zero pattern)
zero_patterns  <- apply(Y_prop > 0, 1, paste, collapse = ",")
pattern_counts <- table(zero_patterns)
log_theta_vec  <- log(as.numeric(pattern_counts[zero_patterns]) / N)
cat(sprintf("\nDistinct zero patterns: %d\n", length(unique(zero_patterns))))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-data
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of prey proportions by season. Most entries are zero."
#| fig-height: 5

Y_long <- as_tibble(Y_prop) |>
  mutate(Season = design_raw$Season) |>
  pivot_longer(-Season, names_to = "prey", values_to = "prop")

ggplot(Y_long, aes(x = reorder(prey, prop, median), y = prop, fill = Season)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, alpha = 0.8, linewidth = 0.3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion", title = "Prey proportions by Season") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Model 1: zoid

```{r}
#| label: fit-zoid
design_zoid   <- design_raw
design_zoid$y <- 1   # dummy response required by formula interface

fit_zoid_null <- fit_zoid(
  data_matrix    = as.matrix(data_raw),
  overdispersion = TRUE,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000, refresh = 500
)

fit_zoid_season <- fit_zoid(
  formula        = y ~ Season,
  design_matrix  = design_zoid,
  data_matrix    = as.matrix(data_raw),
  overdispersion = TRUE,
  chains = 4, 
  iter = 2000, refresh = 500
)
```

## Model 2: Ordered Dirichlet (Single Shared Mean)

The Stan model includes a `generated quantities` block for pointwise log-likelihoods required by `loo`.

```{r}
#| label: stan-code
stan_code <- '
functions {
  real ordered_dirichlet_shared_lpdf(
      vector y, vector theta, real phi, real tau) {
    int K = num_elements(y);
    vector[K] mu  = softmax(theta);
    vector[K] eta = theta - tau;
    int A_size = 0;
    array[K] int active;
    real lp_A      = 0;
    real log_empty = 0;
    for (k in 1:K) {
      real log_rho   = -log1p_exp(-eta[k]);
      real log1m_rho = -log1p_exp(eta[k]);
      log_empty += log1m_rho;
      if (y[k] > 0) {
        A_size += 1; active[A_size] = k; lp_A += log_rho;
      } else {
        lp_A += log1m_rho;
      }
    }
    lp_A -= log1m_exp(log_empty);
    if (A_size == 1) {
      return lp_A;
    } else {
      vector[A_size] y_A;
      vector[A_size] alpha_A;
      real mu_sum = 0;
      for (a in 1:A_size) mu_sum += mu[active[a]];
      for (a in 1:A_size) {
        y_A[a]     = y[active[a]];
        alpha_A[a] = phi * mu[active[a]] / mu_sum;
      }
      return lp_A + dirichlet_lpdf(y_A | alpha_A);
    }
  }
}
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=2> K;
  int<lower=1> P;
  matrix[N, P]       X;
  array[N] vector[K] y;
}
parameters {
  matrix[P, K - 1] beta_raw;
  real tau;
  vector[P] delta;
}
transformed parameters {
  matrix[P, K] beta;
  for (k in 1:(K - 1)) beta[, k] = beta_raw[, k];
  beta[, K] = rep_vector(0, P);
}
model {
  to_vector(beta_raw) ~ normal(0, 1);
  tau   ~ normal(0, 2);
  delta ~ normal(0, 1);
  for (i in 1:N) {
    vector[K] theta_i = beta\' * to_vector(X[i]\');
    real      phi_i   = exp(dot_product(to_vector(X[i]\'), delta));
    y[i] ~ ordered_dirichlet_shared(theta_i, phi_i, tau);
  }
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (i in 1:N) {
    vector[K] theta_i = beta\' * to_vector(X[i]\');
    real      phi_i   = exp(dot_product(to_vector(X[i]\'), delta));
    log_lik[i] = ordered_dirichlet_shared_lpdf(y[i] | theta_i, phi_i, tau);
  }
}
'

stan_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".stan")
writeLines(stan_code, stan_file)
ord_mod <- cmdstan_model(stan_file)
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-ord

X_null   <- matrix(1.0, N, 1L)
X_season <- model.matrix(~ Season, design_raw)   # N x 2: intercept + Season2

shared_args <- list(
  chains = 4L, parallel_chains = 4L,
  iter_warmup = 1000L, iter_sampling = 1000L,
  seed = 123L, refresh = 0L
)

fit_ord_null <- do.call(
  ord_mod$sample,
  c(list(data = list(N = N, K = K, P = 1L, X = X_null,
                     y = lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) Y_prop[i, ]))),
    shared_args)
)

fit_ord_season <- do.call(
  ord_mod$sample,
  c(list(data = list(N = N, K = K, P = ncol(X_season), X = X_season,
                     y = lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) Y_prop[i, ]))),
    shared_args)
)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Model 3: ZADR (Zero-Adjusted Dirichlet Regression)

ZADR uses a multinomial logistic link (softmax) for the Dirichlet mean and treats zeros through an empirical mixture over zero patterns. The `log_theta` vector (log proportion of observations sharing each zero pattern) is passed as fixed data.

```{r}
#| label: fit-zadr
zadr_mod <- cmdstan_model("zadr.stan")

zadr_data_null <- list(
  N         = N,
  K         = K,
  P         = 1L,
  X         = X_null,
  y         = lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) Y_prop[i, ]),
  log_theta = log_theta_vec
)

zadr_data_season <- list(
  N         = N,
  K         = K,
  P         = ncol(X_season),
  X         = X_season,
  y         = lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) Y_prop[i, ]),
  log_theta = log_theta_vec
)

fit_zadr_null <- do.call(
  zadr_mod$sample,
  c(list(data = zadr_data_null), shared_args)
)

fit_zadr_season <- do.call(
  zadr_mod$sample,
  c(list(data = zadr_data_season), shared_args)
)
```

---

## Model 3b: Bayesian ZADR

The Bayesian ZADR replaces the fixed $\theta_b = n_b/N$ plug-in with a
`simplex[B]` parameter estimated from the posterior. A uniform Dirichlet
prior (`alpha_0 = 1`) is used here.

```{r}
#| label: fit-zadr-bayes

# Build integer pattern IDs for each observation
pattern_labels <- apply(Y_prop > 0, 1, paste, collapse = ",")
pattern_levels <- unique(pattern_labels)
B              <- length(pattern_levels)
pattern_id     <- match(pattern_labels, pattern_levels)

cat(sprintf("B = %d distinct zero patterns\n", B))

zadr_bayes_mod <- cmdstan_model("zadr_bayes.stan")

zadr_bayes_data_null <- list(
  N          = N,
  K          = K,
  P          = 1L,
  B          = B,
  X          = X_null,
  y          = lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) Y_prop[i, ]),
  pattern_id = pattern_id,
  alpha_0    = 1.0
)

zadr_bayes_data_season <- list(
  N          = N,
  K          = K,
  P          = ncol(X_season),
  B          = B,
  X          = X_season,
  y          = lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) Y_prop[i, ]),
  pattern_id = pattern_id,
  alpha_0    = 1.0
)

fit_zadr_bayes_null <- do.call(
  zadr_bayes_mod$sample,
  c(list(data = zadr_bayes_data_null), shared_args)
)

fit_zadr_bayes_season <- do.call(
  zadr_bayes_mod$sample,
  c(list(data = zadr_bayes_data_season), shared_args)
)

# Show posterior for theta (zero-pattern probabilities)
theta_summary <- fit_zadr_bayes_season$summary(
  paste0("theta[", seq_len(B), "]")
)
theta_summary$pattern <- pattern_levels
cat("\nPosterior theta (zero-pattern probabilities):\n")
print(theta_summary[, c("variable", "pattern", "mean", "sd", "q5", "q95")])
cat("\nEmpirical theta (n_b/N):\n")
print(table(pattern_labels) / N)
```

## Model 4: Coupled Ordered Dirichlet

The coupled model allows all-zero rows natively and adds an inclusion-scale $a_\rho$. It is fit from `coupled_ordered_dirichlet.stan`.

```{r}
#| label: fit-coupled
coupled_mod <- cmdstan_model("coupled_ordered_dirichlet.stan")

coupled_data_null <- list(
  N   = N,
  K   = K,
  P   = 1L,
  X   = X_null,
  y   = lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) Y_prop[i, ]),
  eps = 1e-10
)

coupled_data_season <- list(
  N   = N,
  K   = K,
  P   = ncol(X_season),
  X   = X_season,
  y   = lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) Y_prop[i, ]),
  eps = 1e-10
)

fit_coupled_null <- do.call(
  coupled_mod$sample,
  c(list(data = coupled_data_null), shared_args)
)

fit_coupled_season <- do.call(
  coupled_mod$sample,
  c(list(data = coupled_data_season), shared_args)
)
```

## LOO Comparison

```{r}
#| label: loo
# zoid stores log_lik at observation×prey granularity (N*K entries); use as-is.
# The ordered Dirichlet model stores one log_lik per observation (N entries),
# since the K prey shares are modeled jointly. To compare at the same N*K
# granularity, we split each observation's log-lik equally across its K prey:
# log_lik_expanded[n, k] = log_lik_obs[n] / K. This preserves total ELPD.
expand_ord_loo <- function(ll_obs, K_prey) {
  N_obs <- ncol(ll_obs)
  ll_expanded <- matrix(0, nrow(ll_obs), N_obs * K_prey)
  for (n in seq_len(N_obs)) {
    cols <- (n - 1L) * K_prey + seq_len(K_prey)
    ll_expanded[, cols] <- ll_obs[, n] / K_prey
  }
  loo::loo(ll_expanded)
}

loo_zoid_null   <- loo::loo(loo::extract_log_lik(fit_zoid_null$model))
loo_zoid_season <- loo::loo(loo::extract_log_lik(fit_zoid_season$model))
loo_ord_null <- expand_ord_loo(
  fit_ord_null$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"), K
)
loo_ord_season <- expand_ord_loo(
  fit_ord_season$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"), K
)
# ZADR (fixed theta): observation-level log_lik (N entries); expand to N*K
loo_zadr_null <- expand_ord_loo(
  fit_zadr_null$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"), K
)
loo_zadr_season <- expand_ord_loo(
  fit_zadr_season$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"), K
)
# Bayesian ZADR: same expansion
loo_zadr_bayes_null <- expand_ord_loo(
  fit_zadr_bayes_null$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"), K
)
loo_zadr_bayes_season <- expand_ord_loo(
  fit_zadr_bayes_season$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"), K
)
# Coupled Ordered Dirichlet: observation-level log_lik; expand to N*K
loo_coupled_null <- expand_ord_loo(
  fit_coupled_null$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"), K
)
loo_coupled_season <- expand_ord_loo(
  fit_coupled_season$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"), K
)

loo_list <- list(
  zoid_null          = loo_zoid_null,
  zoid_season        = loo_zoid_season,
  ord_null           = loo_ord_null,
  ord_season         = loo_ord_season,
  zadr_null          = loo_zadr_null,
  zadr_season        = loo_zadr_season,
  zadr_bayes_null    = loo_zadr_bayes_null,
  zadr_bayes_season  = loo_zadr_bayes_season,
  coupled_null       = loo_coupled_null,
  coupled_season     = loo_coupled_season
)

# Confirm all LOOs see the same N
n_pts <- sapply(loo_list, function(x) nrow(x$pointwise))
cat("Data points per LOO:", paste(names(n_pts), n_pts, sep = "=", collapse = ", "), "\n")

loo_compare(loo_list)
```

## Exact Leave-One-Out Evaluation

PSIS-LOO is an approximation that can be unreliable with small N. Because N = 10 here, we can afford to refit each model 10 times — dropping one row, refitting on the remaining 9, then computing the exact log predictive density for the held-out row.

For each Stan model and each fold $i$, the exact LOO log predictive density is

$$\widehat{\mathrm{lpd}}_i = \log \frac{1}{S}\sum_{s=1}^S p\!\left(y_i \mid \theta^{(s)}\right), \qquad \theta^{(s)} \sim p(\theta \mid y_{-i}),$$

summed to $\mathrm{ELPD} = \sum_i \widehat{\mathrm{lpd}}_i$.

Models included: **Ordered Dirichlet**, **Coupled Ordered Dirichlet**, and **ZADR (fixed θ)**. For ZADR, `log_theta` is recomputed from the training rows at each fold, removing the data-leakage present in the PSIS approximation. zoid is excluded because it models components marginally (no clean joint row density).

```{r}
#| label: exact-loo-helpers

# log-sum-exp stable implementation
lse <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0L) return(-Inf)
  m <- max(x); m + log(sum(exp(x - m)))
}

# R log-density for Ordered Dirichlet (reference = component K)
ord_lpdf_r <- function(y, theta, phi, tau) {
  mu   <- exp(theta - max(theta)); mu <- mu / sum(mu)
  eta  <- theta - tau
  lrho <- plogis( eta, log.p = TRUE)
  l1mr <- plogis(-eta, log.p = TRUE)
  A    <- which(y > 0)
  if (length(A) == 0L) return(-Inf)
  log_empty <- sum(l1mr)
  lp_A <- sum(lrho[A]) + sum(l1mr[-A]) - log1p(-exp(log_empty))
  if (length(A) == 1L) return(lp_A)
  y_A   <- y[A] / sum(y[A])
  mu_A  <- mu[A] / sum(mu[A])
  alpha <- phi * mu_A
  lp_A + lgamma(sum(alpha)) - sum(lgamma(alpha)) + sum((alpha - 1) * log(y_A))
}

# R log-density for Coupled Ordered Dirichlet (reference = component K)
coupled_lpdf_r <- function(y, theta, phi, tau, a_rho, eps = 1e-10) {
  tot  <- sum(y)
  mu   <- exp(theta - max(theta)); mu <- mu / sum(mu)
  eta  <- a_rho * theta - tau
  lrho <- plogis( eta, log.p = TRUE)
  l1mr <- plogis(-eta, log.p = TRUE)
  if (tot <= eps) return(sum(l1mr))
  yn   <- y / tot
  A    <- which(yn > eps)
  lp_A <- sum(lrho[A]) + sum(l1mr[-A])
  if (length(A) == 1L) return(lp_A)
  mu_A  <- mu[A] / sum(mu[A])
  alpha <- phi * mu_A
  lp_A + lgamma(sum(alpha)) - sum(lgamma(alpha)) + sum((alpha - 1) * log(yn[A]))
}

# R log-density for ZADR (reference = component 1)
zadr_lpdf_r <- function(y, mu, phi, log_theta) {
  A <- which(y > 0)
  if (length(A) == 0L) return(-Inf)
  mu_A  <- mu[A] / sum(mu[A])
  alpha <- phi * mu_A
  log_theta + lgamma(phi) - sum(lgamma(alpha)) + sum((alpha - 1) * log(y[A]))
}

# Extract P×K beta from a draws row; reference category = K (ord/coupled)
extr_beta_K <- function(drow, P_s, K_s) {
  cols <- paste0("beta_raw[", rep(seq_len(P_s), K_s - 1L), ",",
                 rep(seq_len(K_s - 1L), each = P_s), "]")
  cbind(matrix(as.numeric(drow[cols]), nrow = P_s, ncol = K_s - 1L), 0)
}

# Extract P×K beta from a draws row; reference category = 1 (ZADR)
extr_beta_1 <- function(drow, P_s, K_s) {
  cols <- paste0("beta_raw[", rep(seq_len(P_s), K_s - 1L), ",",
                 rep(seq_len(K_s - 1L), each = P_s), "]")
  cbind(0, matrix(as.numeric(drow[cols]), nrow = P_s, ncol = K_s - 1L))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: exact-loo
#| cache: true

P_seas <- ncol(X_season)

# Lighter sampling for LOO refits (N-1 = 9 observations)
loo_args <- list(chains = 2L, parallel_chains = 2L,
                 iter_warmup = 500L, iter_sampling = 1000L,
                 seed = 456L, refresh = 0L)

exact_lpd <- vector("list", N)

for (i in seq_len(N)) {
  cat(sprintf("Fold %d / %d\n", i, N))

  train     <- seq_len(N)[-i]
  Y_tr      <- Y_prop[train, , drop = FALSE]
  X_tr      <- X_season[train, , drop = FALSE]
  y_h       <- Y_prop[i, ]
  x_h       <- X_season[i, ]
  y_tr_list <- lapply(seq_len(N - 1L), function(j) Y_tr[j, ])

  # ── Ordered Dirichlet ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  f_ord <- do.call(ord_mod$sample, c(
    list(data = list(N = N - 1L, K = K, P = P_seas,
                     X = X_tr, y = y_tr_list)),
    loo_args))
  d_ord <- f_ord$draws(c("beta_raw", "tau", "delta"), format = "df") |>
    select(-starts_with("."))

  lp_ord <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(d_ord)), function(s) {
    b   <- extr_beta_K(d_ord[s, ], P_seas, K)
    tau <- as.numeric(d_ord$tau[s])
    del <- as.numeric(d_ord[s, paste0("delta[", seq_len(P_seas), "]")])
    ord_lpdf_r(y_h, as.vector(t(b) %*% x_h), exp(sum(del * x_h)), tau)
  }, numeric(1L))

  # ── Coupled Ordered Dirichlet ────────────────────────────────────────────
  f_cpl <- do.call(coupled_mod$sample, c(
    list(data = list(N = N - 1L, K = K, P = P_seas,
                     X = X_tr, y = y_tr_list, eps = 1e-10)),
    loo_args))
  d_cpl <- f_cpl$draws(c("beta_raw", "tau", "a_rho", "delta"), format = "df") |>
    select(-starts_with("."))

  lp_cpl <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(d_cpl)), function(s) {
    b    <- extr_beta_K(d_cpl[s, ], P_seas, K)
    tau  <- as.numeric(d_cpl$tau[s])
    arho <- as.numeric(d_cpl$a_rho[s])
    del  <- as.numeric(d_cpl[s, paste0("delta[", seq_len(P_seas), "]")])
    coupled_lpdf_r(y_h, as.vector(t(b) %*% x_h), exp(sum(del * x_h)), tau, arho)
  }, numeric(1L))

  # ── ZADR (log_theta recomputed from training rows only) ──────────────────
  tr_pats   <- apply(Y_tr > 0, 1, paste, collapse = ",")
  tr_counts <- table(tr_pats)
  lth_tr    <- log(as.numeric(tr_counts[tr_pats]) / (N - 1L))
  h_pat     <- paste(y_h > 0, collapse = ",")
  lth_h     <- if (h_pat %in% names(tr_counts))
                 log(as.numeric(tr_counts[h_pat]) / (N - 1L))
               else
                 log(1 / N)   # unseen pattern: assign 1/N probability

  f_zad <- do.call(zadr_mod$sample, c(
    list(data = list(N = N - 1L, K = K, P = P_seas,
                     X = X_tr, y = y_tr_list, log_theta = lth_tr)),
    loo_args))
  d_zad <- f_zad$draws(c("beta_raw", "phi"), format = "df") |>
    select(-starts_with("."))

  lp_zad <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(d_zad)), function(s) {
    b   <- extr_beta_1(d_zad[s, ], P_seas, K)
    phi <- as.numeric(d_zad$phi[s])
    mu  <- exp(as.vector(t(b) %*% x_h)); mu <- mu / sum(mu)
    zadr_lpdf_r(y_h, mu, phi, lth_h)
  }, numeric(1L))

  exact_lpd[[i]] <- data.frame(
    fold  = i,
    model = c("Ordered Dirichlet", "Coupled Ord. Dirichlet", "ZADR (fixed θ)"),
    lpd   = c(lse(lp_ord) - log(length(lp_ord)),
              lse(lp_cpl) - log(length(lp_cpl)),
              lse(lp_zad) - log(length(lp_zad)))
  )
}

exact_lpd_df <- do.call(rbind, exact_lpd)
```

```{r}
  summarise(
```

## Posterior Predictive Checks

We compare each model's ability to reproduce two key features of the observed data: (1) the mean proportion per prey item and (2) the proportion of zero entries per prey item.

```{r}
#| label: ppc-helpers

# rdirichlet for simulation
rdirichlet <- function(n, alpha) {
  k <- length(alpha)
  x <- matrix(rgamma(n * k, rep(alpha, each = n)), nrow = n, ncol = k)
  x / rowSums(x)
}

# Simulate from ordered dirichlet given beta (P x K), tau, delta, X
sim_ord <- function(X, beta, tau, delta) {
  N_s <- nrow(X)
  K_s <- ncol(beta)
  Y   <- matrix(0.0, N_s, K_s)
  for (i in seq_len(N_s)) {
    theta_i <- as.vector(t(beta) %*% X[i, ])
    phi_i   <- exp(sum(delta * X[i, ]))
    mu_i    <- exp(theta_i - max(theta_i)); mu_i <- mu_i / sum(mu_i)
    rho_i   <- plogis(theta_i - tau)
    repeat {
      active <- rbinom(K_s, 1L, rho_i) == 1L
      if (any(active)) break
    }
    idx <- which(active)
    if (length(idx) == 1L) {
      Y[i, idx] <- 1.0
    } else {
      mu_a <- mu_i[idx] / sum(mu_i[idx])
      Y[i, idx] <- rdirichlet(1L, phi_i * mu_a)
    }
  }
  Y
}

# Summarise Y_rep: mean proportion + P(zero) per prey
summarise_y <- function(Y_mat, prey_nms) {
  tibble(
    prey      = rep(prey_nms, 2),
    stat      = rep(c("Mean proportion", "P(zero)"), each = length(prey_nms)),
    value     = c(colMeans(Y_mat), colMeans(Y_mat == 0))
  )
}

obs_summary <- summarise_y(Y_prop, prey_names) |> rename(obs = value)

# Simulate from coupled ordered Dirichlet: beta (P x K), a_rho, tau, delta
sim_coupled <- function(X, beta, a_rho, tau, delta) {
  N_s <- nrow(X)
  K_s <- ncol(beta)
  Y   <- matrix(0.0, N_s, K_s)
  for (i in seq_len(N_s)) {
    theta_i <- as.vector(t(beta) %*% X[i, ])
    phi_i   <- exp(sum(delta * X[i, ]))
    mu_i    <- exp(theta_i - max(theta_i)); mu_i <- mu_i / sum(mu_i)
    rho_i   <- plogis(a_rho * theta_i - tau)
    z       <- rbinom(K_s, 1L, rho_i)
    A       <- which(z == 1L)
    if (length(A) == 0L) {
      # all-zero row
    } else if (length(A) == 1L) {
      Y[i, A] <- 1.0
    } else {
      mu_A    <- mu_i[A] / sum(mu_i[A])
      Y[i, A] <- rdirichlet(1L, phi_i * mu_A)
    }
  }
  Y
}

# Simulate one replicate from ZADR given beta (P x K), phi, and observed Y
sim_zadr <- function(X, beta, phi, Y_obs) {
  N_s <- nrow(X)
  K_s <- ncol(beta)
  Y   <- matrix(0.0, N_s, K_s)
  for (i in seq_len(N_s)) {
    mu_full <- as.vector(exp(t(beta) %*% X[i, ]))
    mu_full <- mu_full / sum(mu_full)
    active  <- Y_obs[i, ] > 0
    if (!any(active)) active[which.max(mu_full)] <- TRUE
    if (sum(active) == 1L) {
      Y[i, active] <- 1.0
    } else {
      mu_act      <- mu_full[active] / sum(mu_full[active])
      Y[i, active] <- rdirichlet(1L, phi * mu_act)
    }
  }
  Y
}
```

### zoid

```{r}
#| label: ppc-zoid
S_ppc <- 100L

# zoid: use get_fitted() for posterior mean predictions per observation
fitted_season <- get_fitted(fit_zoid_season)

# get_fitted returns obs/group/mean per prey.
# group may be a numeric index (1:K) rather than a prey name, so we map
# by position (zoid preserves column order from data_raw).
zoid_wide <- fitted_season |>
  select(obs, group, mean) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = mean) |>
  select(-obs)
stopifnot(ncol(zoid_wide) == K)
colnames(zoid_wide) <- prey_names          # map by position
zoid_mean_mat <- as.matrix(zoid_wide)

# For PPC replications sample from the posterior predictive draws of zoid
# zoid stores draws as log_lik only; use posterior mean as point PPC overlay
zoid_ppc_summary <- summarise_y(zoid_mean_mat, prey_names) |>
  rename(pred = value)
```

### Ordered Dirichlet

```{r}
#| label: ppc-ord
draws_season <- fit_ord_season$draws(c("beta_raw", "tau", "delta"),
                                      format = "df") |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |>
  slice_sample(n = S_ppc)

P_s <- ncol(X_season)

ord_ppc_rows    <- vector("list", S_ppc)
yrep_ord_full   <- matrix(0.0, nrow = S_ppc, ncol = N * K)  # S × (N*K), column-major

for (s in seq_len(S_ppc)) {
  br_cols <- paste0("beta_raw[", rep(seq_len(P_s), K - 1L), ",",
                    rep(seq_len(K - 1L), each = P_s), "]")
  beta_s  <- cbind(
    matrix(as.numeric(draws_season[s, br_cols]), nrow = P_s, ncol = K - 1L),
    0
  )
  tau_s   <- as.numeric(draws_season$tau[s])
  delta_s <- as.numeric(draws_season[s, paste0("delta[", seq_len(P_s), "]")])

  Y_rep <- sim_ord(X_season, beta_s, tau_s, delta_s)
  yrep_ord_full[s, ] <- as.vector(Y_rep)   # column-major: prey k in cols (k-1)*N+1 : k*N

  ord_ppc_rows[[s]] <- data.frame(
    draw  = s,
    prey  = rep(prey_names, 2),
    stat  = rep(c("Mean proportion", "P(zero)"), each = K),
    value = c(colMeans(Y_rep), colMeans(Y_rep == 0))
  )
}
ord_ppc_df <- do.call(rbind, ord_ppc_rows)
```

### ZADR

```{r}
#| label: ppc-zadr
P_zadr <- ncol(X_season)

zadr_ppc_rows  <- vector("list", S_ppc)
yrep_zadr_full <- matrix(0.0, nrow = S_ppc, ncol = N * K)

draws_zadr <- fit_zadr_season$draws(c("beta_raw", "phi"), format = "df") |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |>
  slice_sample(n = S_ppc)

for (s in seq_len(S_ppc)) {
  br_cols  <- paste0("beta_raw[", rep(seq_len(P_zadr), K - 1L), ",",
                     rep(seq_len(K - 1L), each = P_zadr), "]")
  # ZADR: beta[,1] = 0 (reference), beta[,2:K] = beta_raw[,1:(K-1)]
  beta_s   <- cbind(
    rep(0, P_zadr),
    matrix(as.numeric(draws_zadr[s, br_cols]), nrow = P_zadr, ncol = K - 1L)
  )
  phi_s    <- as.numeric(draws_zadr$phi[s])

  Y_rep <- sim_zadr(X_season, beta_s, phi_s, Y_prop)
  yrep_zadr_full[s, ] <- as.vector(Y_rep)

  zadr_ppc_rows[[s]] <- data.frame(
    draw  = s,
    prey  = rep(prey_names, 2),
    stat  = rep(c("Mean proportion", "P(zero)"), each = K),
    value = c(colMeans(Y_rep), colMeans(Y_rep == 0))
  )
}
zadr_ppc_df <- do.call(rbind, zadr_ppc_rows)
yrep_zadr_full[!is.finite(yrep_zadr_full)] <- 0
```

### Bayesian ZADR

```{r}
#| label: ppc-zadr-bayes

zadr_bayes_ppc_rows  <- vector("list", S_ppc)
yrep_zadr_bayes_full <- matrix(0.0, nrow = S_ppc, ncol = N * K)

draws_zadr_bayes <- fit_zadr_bayes_season$draws(
  c("beta_raw", "phi", paste0("theta[", seq_len(B), "]")),
  format = "df"
) |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |>
  slice_sample(n = S_ppc)

for (s in seq_len(S_ppc)) {
  br_cols_b <- paste0("beta_raw[", rep(seq_len(P_zadr), K - 1L), ",",
                      rep(seq_len(K - 1L), each = P_zadr), "]")
  beta_sb <- cbind(
    rep(0, P_zadr),
    matrix(as.numeric(draws_zadr_bayes[s, br_cols_b]), nrow = P_zadr, ncol = K - 1L)
  )
  phi_sb   <- as.numeric(draws_zadr_bayes$phi[s])
  # Compute per-observation log_theta from this draw's theta simplex
  theta_sb <- as.numeric(draws_zadr_bayes[s, paste0("theta[", seq_len(B), "]")])
  log_theta_sb <- log(theta_sb[pattern_id])

  Y_rep <- matrix(0.0, N, K)
  for (i in seq_len(N)) {
    mu_full <- as.vector(exp(t(beta_sb) %*% X_season[i, ]))
    mu_full <- mu_full / sum(mu_full)
    active  <- Y_prop[i, ] > 0
    if (!any(active)) active[which.max(mu_full)] <- TRUE
    if (sum(active) == 1L) {
      Y_rep[i, active] <- 1.0
    } else {
      mu_act           <- mu_full[active] / sum(mu_full[active])
      Y_rep[i, active] <- rdirichlet(1L, phi_sb * mu_act)
    }
  }
  yrep_zadr_bayes_full[s, ] <- as.vector(Y_rep)

  zadr_bayes_ppc_rows[[s]] <- data.frame(
    draw  = s,
    prey  = rep(prey_names, 2),
    stat  = rep(c("Mean proportion", "P(zero)"), each = K),
    value = c(colMeans(Y_rep), colMeans(Y_rep == 0))
  )
}
zadr_bayes_ppc_df <- do.call(rbind, zadr_bayes_ppc_rows)
yrep_zadr_bayes_full[!is.finite(yrep_zadr_bayes_full)] <- 0
```

### Coupled Ordered Dirichlet

```{r}
#| label: ppc-coupled
P_coupled <- ncol(X_season)

coupled_ppc_rows  <- vector("list", S_ppc)
yrep_coupled_full <- matrix(0.0, nrow = S_ppc, ncol = N * K)

draws_coupled <- fit_coupled_season$draws(
  c("beta_raw", "tau", "a_rho", "delta"),
  format = "df"
) |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |>
  slice_sample(n = S_ppc)

for (s in seq_len(S_ppc)) {
  br_cols_c <- paste0("beta_raw[", rep(seq_len(P_coupled), K - 1L), ",",
                      rep(seq_len(K - 1L), each = P_coupled), "]")
  # Coupled: reference category is K (beta[,K] = 0)
  beta_sc <- cbind(
    matrix(as.numeric(draws_coupled[s, br_cols_c]), nrow = P_coupled, ncol = K - 1L),
    0
  )
  tau_sc   <- as.numeric(draws_coupled$tau[s])
  a_rho_sc <- as.numeric(draws_coupled$a_rho[s])
  delta_sc <- as.numeric(draws_coupled[s, paste0("delta[", seq_len(P_coupled), "]")])

  Y_rep <- sim_coupled(X_season, beta_sc, a_rho_sc, tau_sc, delta_sc)
  yrep_coupled_full[s, ] <- as.vector(Y_rep)

  coupled_ppc_rows[[s]] <- data.frame(
    draw  = s,
    prey  = rep(prey_names, 2),
    stat  = rep(c("Mean proportion", "P(zero)"), each = K),
    value = c(colMeans(Y_rep), colMeans(Y_rep == 0))
  )
}
coupled_ppc_df <- do.call(rbind, coupled_ppc_rows)
yrep_coupled_full[!is.finite(yrep_coupled_full)] <- 0
```

## Predictive Performance: RMSE and Classification

```{r}
#| label: perf-metrics

# ── Zoid posterior predictive draws ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Try to extract y_rep from the rstan fit; simulate if not present.
zoid_par_names <- names(rstan::extract(fit_zoid_season$model))
cat("zoid generated quantities:", paste(grep("y_rep|yrep", zoid_par_names,
                                              value = TRUE), collapse = ", "), "\n")

if (any(grepl("^y_rep$", zoid_par_names))) {
  y_rep_z <- rstan::extract(fit_zoid_season$model, "y_rep")$y_rep
  # shape S × N × K  → subsample and vectorise
  idx_z          <- sample(dim(y_rep_z)[1], S_ppc)
  yrep_zoid_full <- t(apply(y_rep_z[idx_z, , , drop = FALSE], 1L, as.vector))
  cat("Using y_rep from zoid Stan model.\n")
} else {
  # Fallback: use rstan::extract() to get raw draws, or simulate from
  # per-observation posterior means when individual draws are unavailable.
  all_draws_z    <- rstan::extract(fit_zoid_season$model)
  zoid_all_names <- names(all_draws_z)
  cat("zoid Stan parameters:", paste(head(zoid_all_names, 15), collapse = ", "), "\n")

  # zoid typically stores theta (N × K log-mean) and phi (overdispersion)
  theta_candidates <- grep("^theta|^mu|^p$|^alpha", zoid_all_names, value = TRUE)

  if (length(theta_candidates) > 0L) {
    theta_nm  <- theta_candidates[1L]
    theta_arr <- all_draws_z[[theta_nm]]          # S × N × K  (or S × K)
    phi_arr   <- if ("phi_vec" %in% zoid_all_names) all_draws_z$phi_vec
                 else if ("phi" %in% zoid_all_names) all_draws_z$phi
                 else rep(1, dim(theta_arr)[1])

    idx_z <- sample(dim(theta_arr)[1], S_ppc, replace = TRUE)
    yrep_zoid_full <- matrix(0.0, S_ppc, N * K)
    for (s in seq_len(S_ppc)) {
      th_s  <- if (length(dim(theta_arr)) == 3L) theta_arr[idx_z[s], , ]
               else matrix(theta_arr[idx_z[s], ], N, K, byrow = TRUE)
      ph_s  <- if (length(phi_arr) >= idx_z[s]) phi_arr[idx_z[s]] else 1
      Y_z   <- matrix(0.0, N, K)
      for (i in seq_len(N)) {
        mu_i  <- exp(th_s[i, ]); mu_i <- mu_i / sum(mu_i)
        rho_i <- pmin(pmax(mu_i * K / 2, 0.05), 0.95)
        repeat { active <- rbinom(K, 1L, rho_i) == 1L; if (any(active)) break }
        idx_a <- which(active)
        if (length(idx_a) == 1L) { Y_z[i, idx_a] <- 1
        } else {
          a <- pmax(ph_s * mu_i[idx_a], 1e-4)
          Y_z[i, idx_a] <- rdirichlet(1L, a)
        }
      }
      yrep_zoid_full[s, ] <- as.vector(Y_z)
    }
    cat("Simulated zoid PPC from rstan theta draws.\n")
  } else {
    # Last resort: simulate around per-observation posterior means
    # (uncertainty is from Dirichlet sampling only, not posterior parameter draws)
    phi_summary  <- get_pars(fit_zoid_season)
    phi_val      <- tryCatch(median(phi_summary$phi$mean, na.rm = TRUE),
                             error = function(e) 1.0)
    if (is.na(phi_val) || !is.finite(phi_val)) phi_val <- 1.0

    yrep_zoid_full <- matrix(0.0, S_ppc, N * K)
    for (s in seq_len(S_ppc)) {
      Y_z <- matrix(0.0, N, K)
      for (i in seq_len(N)) {
        mu_i  <- pmax(zoid_mean_mat[i, ], 1e-8); mu_i <- mu_i / sum(mu_i)
        rho_i <- pmin(pmax(mu_i * K / 2, 0.05), 0.95)
        repeat { active <- rbinom(K, 1L, rho_i) == 1L; if (any(active)) break }
        idx_a <- which(active)
        if (length(idx_a) == 1L) { Y_z[i, idx_a] <- 1
        } else {
          a <- pmax(phi_val * mu_i[idx_a], 1e-4)
          Y_z[i, idx_a] <- rdirichlet(1L, a)
        }
      }
      yrep_zoid_full[s, ] <- as.vector(Y_z)
    }
    cat("Simulated zoid PPC from posterior mean + Dirichlet noise (approximate).\n")
  }
}

# Sanitise: replace any NaN/Inf in zoid predictions with 0
yrep_zoid_full[!is.finite(yrep_zoid_full)] <- 0

# ── RMSE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rmse_ord  <- apply(yrep_ord_full,  1L, function(yh) sqrt(mean((yh - y_obs_vec)^2)))
rmse_zoid <- apply(yrep_zoid_full, 1L, function(yh) sqrt(mean((yh - y_obs_vec)^2)))
rmse_zadr       <- apply(yrep_zadr_full,       1L, function(yh) sqrt(mean((yh - y_obs_vec)^2)))
rmse_zadr_bayes <- apply(yrep_zadr_bayes_full, 1L, function(yh) sqrt(mean((yh - y_obs_vec)^2)))
rmse_coupled    <- apply(yrep_coupled_full,    1L, function(yh) sqrt(mean((yh - y_obs_vec)^2)))

# ── Percent correctly classified (zero vs non-zero) ──────────────────────────
pcc_ord  <- apply(yrep_ord_full,  1L, function(yh) mean((yh > 0) == (y_obs_vec > 0)))
pcc_zoid <- apply(yrep_zoid_full, 1L, function(yh) mean((yh > 0) == (y_obs_vec > 0)))
pcc_zadr       <- apply(yrep_zadr_full,       1L, function(yh) mean((yh > 0) == (y_obs_vec > 0)))
pcc_zadr_bayes <- apply(yrep_zadr_bayes_full, 1L, function(yh) mean((yh > 0) == (y_obs_vec > 0)))
pcc_coupled    <- apply(yrep_coupled_full,    1L, function(yh) mean((yh > 0) == (y_obs_vec > 0)))

q <- function(x, p) quantile(x, p, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("\nOrdered Dirichlet      — RMSE: %.4f [%.4f, %.4f]  PCC: %.3f [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
            median(rmse_ord, na.rm=TRUE), q(rmse_ord, .05), q(rmse_ord, .95),
            median(pcc_ord,  na.rm=TRUE), q(pcc_ord,  .05), q(pcc_ord,  .95)))
cat(sprintf("Coupled Ord. Dirichlet — RMSE: %.4f [%.4f, %.4f]  PCC: %.3f [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
            median(rmse_coupled, na.rm=TRUE), q(rmse_coupled, .05), q(rmse_coupled, .95),
            median(pcc_coupled,  na.rm=TRUE), q(pcc_coupled,  .05), q(pcc_coupled,  .95)))
cat(sprintf("ZADR (fixed θ)         — RMSE: %.4f [%.4f, %.4f]  PCC: %.3f [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
            median(rmse_zadr, na.rm=TRUE), q(rmse_zadr, .05), q(rmse_zadr, .95),
            median(pcc_zadr,  na.rm=TRUE), q(pcc_zadr,  .05), q(pcc_zadr,  .95)))
cat(sprintf("ZADR (Bayes θ)         — RMSE: %.4f [%.4f, %.4f]  PCC: %.3f [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
            median(rmse_zadr_bayes, na.rm=TRUE), q(rmse_zadr_bayes, .05), q(rmse_zadr_bayes, .95),
            median(pcc_zadr_bayes,  na.rm=TRUE), q(pcc_zadr_bayes,  .05), q(pcc_zadr_bayes,  .95)))
cat(sprintf("zoid                   — RMSE: %.4f [%.4f, %.4f]  PCC: %.3f [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
            median(rmse_zoid, na.rm=TRUE), q(rmse_zoid, .05), q(rmse_zoid, .95),
            median(pcc_zoid,  na.rm=TRUE), q(pcc_zoid,  .05), q(pcc_zoid,  .95)))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-rmse-pcc
#| fig-cap: "Posterior predictive RMSE and percent correctly classified (zero vs non-zero) across 100 draws. Overlapping distributions indicate similar predictive accuracy."
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 9

perf_df <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(model = "Ordered Dirichlet",      metric = "RMSE", value = rmse_ord),
  data.frame(model = "Coupled Ord. Dirichlet", metric = "RMSE", value = rmse_coupled),

  data.frame(model = "ZADR (Bayes θ)",         metric = "RMSE", value = rmse_zadr_bayes),
  data.frame(model = "zoid",                   metric = "RMSE", value = rmse_zoid),
  data.frame(model = "Ordered Dirichlet",      metric = "PCC (zero vs non-zero)",
             value = pcc_ord),
  data.frame(model = "Coupled Ord. Dirichlet", metric = "PCC (zero vs non-zero)",
             value = pcc_coupled),
  data.frame(model = "ZADR (fixed θ)",         metric = "PCC (zero vs non-zero)",
             value = pcc_zadr),
  data.frame(model = "ZADR (Bayes θ)",         metric = "PCC (zero vs non-zero)",
             value = pcc_zadr_bayes),
  data.frame(model = "zoid",                   metric = "PCC (zero vs non-zero)",
             value = pcc_zoid)
)

ggplot(perf_df, aes(x = value, fill = model, colour = model)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4, linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density", fill = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Predictive performance distributions (100 posterior draws)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Three-way Predictive Decomposition

Every entry $y_{ik}$ falls into exactly one of three regions: a structural zero
($y = 0$), a concentrated one ($y = 1$, meaning the entire composition is in
that single category for that observation), or a continuous interior value
($0 < y < 1$). The plot below compares how much mass each model's posterior
predictive distribution places in each region against the observed data.

```{r}
#| label: mix-props

# Per-draw proportions of zeros, ones, and interior values across all N*K cells
mix_props <- function(yrep, eps = 1e-9) {
  t(apply(yrep, 1L, function(row) c(
    `Zero (y = 0)`         = mean(row <= eps),
    `One (y = 1)`          = mean(row >= 1 - eps),
    `Interior (0 < y < 1)` = mean(row > eps & row < 1 - eps)
  )))
}

mix_ord        <- mix_props(yrep_ord_full)
mix_zoid       <- mix_props(yrep_zoid_full)
mix_zadr       <- mix_props(yrep_zadr_full)
mix_zadr_bayes <- mix_props(yrep_zadr_bayes_full)
mix_coupled    <- mix_props(yrep_coupled_full)

obs_mix <- c(
  `Zero (y = 0)`         = mean(y_obs_vec <= 1e-9),
  `One (y = 1)`          = mean(y_obs_vec >= 1 - 1e-9),
  `Interior (0 < y < 1)` = mean(y_obs_vec > 1e-9 & y_obs_vec < 1 - 1e-9)
)

cat("Observed proportions:\n")
print(round(obs_mix, 4))
cat("\nPosterior predictive medians [90% CI]:\n")
for (nm in c("Ordered Dirichlet", "Coupled Ord. Dirichlet", "zoid",
             "ZADR (fixed θ)", "ZADR (Bayes θ)")) {
  mx <- switch(nm,
    "Ordered Dirichlet"      = mix_ord,
    "Coupled Ord. Dirichlet" = mix_coupled,
    "zoid"                   = mix_zoid,
    "ZADR (fixed θ)"         = mix_zadr,
    "ZADR (Bayes θ)"         = mix_zadr_bayes
  )
  cat(sprintf("  %-20s  zero=%.3f [%.3f,%.3f]  one=%.3f [%.3f,%.3f]  interior=%.3f [%.3f,%.3f]\n",
    nm,
    median(mx[,1]), quantile(mx[,1],.05), quantile(mx[,1],.95),
    median(mx[,2]), quantile(mx[,2],.05), quantile(mx[,2],.95),
    median(mx[,3]), quantile(mx[,3],.05), quantile(mx[,3],.95)
  ))
}

mix_df <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(mix_ord)        |> mutate(model = "Ordered Dirichlet"),
  as.data.frame(mix_coupled)    |> mutate(model = "Coupled Ord. Dirichlet"),
  as.data.frame(mix_zoid)       |> mutate(model = "zoid"),
  as.data.frame(mix_zadr)       |> mutate(model = "ZADR (fixed θ)"),
  as.data.frame(mix_zadr_bayes) |> mutate(model = "ZADR (Bayes θ)")
) |>
  pivot_longer(-model, names_to = "component", values_to = "proportion") |>
  mutate(component = factor(component,
    levels = c("Zero (y = 0)", "One (y = 1)", "Interior (0 < y < 1)")))

obs_df <- data.frame(
  component  = factor(names(obs_mix),
    levels = c("Zero (y = 0)", "One (y = 1)", "Interior (0 < y < 1)")),
  proportion = as.numeric(obs_mix)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-mix-props
#| fig-cap: "Posterior predictive proportion of zeros, ones, and interior (0,1) values per model across all N×K observation–prey cells. Distributions are over 100 draws; dashed red line = observed proportion. Because ZADR conditions on the observed zero pattern, its zero distribution collapses to a spike at the observed fraction."
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 11

ggplot(mix_df, aes(x = proportion, fill = model, colour = model)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.7, trim = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(data = obs_df, aes(xintercept = proportion),
             colour = "red", linewidth = 0.9, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ component, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(x = "Proportion of all N×K cells", y = "Density",
       fill = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Three-way decomposition of posterior predictive values") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4

  x    = seq_len(N),
  prob = 0.5, prob_outer = 0.9
) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Posterior predictive intervals: %s", prey_names[k_show]),
```

## Comparing Expected Proportions by Season

Here we directly compare the Season-level predictions from each model.

```{r}
#| label: fig-season-preds
#| fig-cap: "Model-predicted mean proportion per prey item by Season. Points are posterior means; segments span the 90% CI."
#| fig-height: 6

# zoid predictions (get_fitted returns per-observation; average by Season).
# group is a positional index — map to prey_names before summarising.
zoid_fitted_long <- get_fitted(fit_zoid_season) |>
  mutate(
    Season = design_raw$Season[obs],
    prey   = prey_names[as.integer(group)]
  ) |>
  group_by(prey, Season) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(mean), lo = mean(lo), hi = mean(hi), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(model = "zoid")

# Ordered Dirichlet: simulate from the posterior predictive for each Season.
# Using simulation (rather than 2^K subset enumeration) is robust to any K.
# For each draw and each Season level, simulate N_sim observations and average.

sim_ord_single <- function(theta, phi, tau, n_sim = 200L) {
  K_s <- length(theta)
  mu  <- exp(theta - max(theta)); mu <- mu / sum(mu)
  rho <- plogis(theta - tau)
  Y   <- matrix(0.0, n_sim, K_s)
  for (i in seq_len(n_sim)) {
    repeat {
      active <- rbinom(K_s, 1L, rho) == 1L
      if (any(active)) break
    }
    idx <- which(active)
    if (length(idx) == 1L) {
      Y[i, idx] <- 1.0
    } else {
      mu_a <- mu[idx] / sum(mu[idx])
      Y[i, idx] <- rdirichlet(1L, phi * mu_a)
    }
  }
  colMeans(Y)
}

seasons   <- levels(design_raw$Season)
X_newdata <- model.matrix(~ Season,
              data.frame(Season = factor(seasons, levels = seasons)))

S_me <- 200L
draws_me <- fit_ord_season$draws(c("beta_raw", "tau", "delta"), format = "df") |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |>
  slice_sample(n = S_me)

ord_me_rows <- vector("list", S_me * length(seasons))
idx_r <- 1L
for (s in seq_len(S_me)) {
  br_cols <- paste0("beta_raw[", rep(seq_len(P_s), K - 1L), ",",
                    rep(seq_len(K - 1L), each = P_s), "]")
  beta_s  <- cbind(
    matrix(as.numeric(draws_me[s, br_cols]), nrow = P_s, ncol = K - 1L),
    0
  )
  tau_s   <- as.numeric(draws_me$tau[s])
  delta_s <- as.numeric(draws_me[s, paste0("delta[", seq_len(P_s), "]")])
  for (j in seq_along(seasons)) {
    theta_j <- as.vector(t(beta_s) %*% X_newdata[j, ])
    phi_j   <- exp(sum(delta_s * X_newdata[j, ]))
    E_j     <- sim_ord_single(theta_j, phi_j, tau_s)
    ord_me_rows[[idx_r]] <- data.frame(
      draw = s, Season = seasons[j],
      prey = prey_names, E_y = E_j
    )
    idx_r <- idx_r + 1L
  }
}
ord_me_df <- do.call(rbind, ord_me_rows)

ord_season_summary <- ord_me_df |>
  group_by(Season, prey) |>
  summarise(mean = median(E_y),
            lo   = quantile(E_y, 0.05),
            hi   = quantile(E_y, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(model = "Ordered Dirichlet")

# Coupled Ordered Dirichlet season predictions
sim_coupled_single <- function(theta, phi, a_rho, tau, n_sim = 200L) {
  K_s <- length(theta)
  mu  <- exp(theta - max(theta)); mu <- mu / sum(mu)
  rho <- plogis(a_rho * theta - tau)
  Y   <- matrix(0.0, n_sim, K_s)
  for (i in seq_len(n_sim)) {
    z <- rbinom(K_s, 1L, rho)
    A <- which(z == 1L)
    if (length(A) == 0L) {
      # all-zero row
    } else if (length(A) == 1L) {
      Y[i, A] <- 1.0
    } else {
      mu_a    <- mu[A] / sum(mu[A])
      Y[i, A] <- rdirichlet(1L, phi * mu_a)
    }
  }
  colMeans(Y)
}

draws_coupled_me <- fit_coupled_season$draws(
  c("beta_raw", "tau", "a_rho", "delta"),
  format = "df"
) |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |>
  slice_sample(n = S_me)

coupled_me_rows <- vector("list", S_me * length(seasons))

for (s in seq_len(S_me)) {
  br_cols_c2 <- paste0("beta_raw[", rep(seq_len(P_coupled), K - 1L), ",",
                       rep(seq_len(K - 1L), each = P_coupled), "]")
  beta_sc2 <- cbind(
    matrix(as.numeric(draws_coupled_me[s, br_cols_c2]), nrow = P_coupled, ncol = K - 1L),
    0
  )
  tau_sc2   <- as.numeric(draws_coupled_me$tau[s])
  a_rho_sc2 <- as.numeric(draws_coupled_me$a_rho[s])
  delta_sc2 <- as.numeric(draws_coupled_me[s, paste0("delta[", seq_len(P_coupled), "]")])
  for (j in seq_along(seasons)) {
    theta_j3 <- as.vector(t(beta_sc2) %*% X_newdata[j, ])
    phi_j3   <- exp(sum(delta_sc2 * X_newdata[j, ]))
    E_j3     <- sim_coupled_single(theta_j3, phi_j3, a_rho_sc2, tau_sc2)
    coupled_me_rows[[idx_r4]] <- data.frame(
      draw = s, Season = seasons[j],
      prey = prey_names, E_y = E_j3
    )
    idx_r4 <- idx_r4 + 1L
  }
}
coupled_me_df <- do.call(rbind, coupled_me_rows)

coupled_season_summary <- coupled_me_df |>
  group_by(Season, prey) |>
  summarise(mean = median(E_y),
            lo   = quantile(E_y, 0.05),
            hi   = quantile(E_y, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(model = "Coupled Ord. Dirichlet")

# ZADR season predictions: simulate from posterior predictive for each Season.
# Zero pattern is drawn empirically from observed patterns (theta_b = n_b/N).
sim_zadr_single <- function(theta, phi, n_sim = 200L) {
  mu_full <- exp(theta - max(theta)); mu_full <- mu_full / sum(mu_full)
  K_s <- length(theta)
  Y   <- matrix(0.0, n_sim, K_s)
  # Sample zero patterns from empirical distribution
  pattern_rows <- sample(N, n_sim, replace = TRUE)
  for (i in seq_len(n_sim)) {
    active <- Y_prop[pattern_rows[i], ] > 0
    if (!any(active)) active[which.max(mu_full)] <- TRUE
    if (sum(active) == 1L) {
      Y[i, active] <- 1.0
    } else {
      mu_act      <- mu_full[active] / sum(mu_full[active])
      Y[i, active] <- rdirichlet(1L, phi * mu_act)
    }
  }
  colMeans(Y)
}

draws_zadr_me <- fit_zadr_season$draws(c("beta_raw", "phi"), format = "df") |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |>
  slice_sample(n = S_me)

      draw = s, Season = seasons[j],
      prey = prey_names, E_y = E_j

    idx_r2 <- idx_r2 + 1L
  }
}

  summarise(mean = median(E_y),
```

## Simulation: Covariate-Driven Zero Patterns

ZADR's advantage in the LOO analysis above rests on the assumption that training zero patterns are representative of test zero patterns. This simulation breaks that assumption: the DGP (a coupled ordered Dirichlet) makes zero patterns **shift with a continuous covariate** $x$. We train on $x \le 0.5$ and test on $x > 0.5$, so the test set contains zero patterns never seen in training. ZADR must fall back to $\log(1/N_\text{train})$ for every test observation; the ordered Dirichlet and coupled model can generalise because they model inclusion through the covariate.

```{r}
#| label: sim-dgp

# ── DGP parameters ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
N_sim  <- 300L
K_sim  <- 6L
P_sim  <- 2L    # intercept + x

# Prey 1–2 activate at low x; prey 4–5 activate at high x; prey 3 & 6 neutral
beta_sim <- rbind(
  intercept = c(-1, -0.5,  0.2,  0.2, -0.5, 0),   # last col = 0 (reference)
  x_effect  = c(-4,  -3,   0.5,   3,   4,   0)
)
delta_sim  <- c(log(8), 0)   # phi ~ 8, flat across x
tau_sim    <- 0
a_rho_sim  <- 1.5

# Simulate from the coupled ordered Dirichlet DGP
set.seed(42)
x_sim_raw <- runif(N_sim)
X_sim_raw <- cbind(1, x_sim_raw)

Y_sim_raw <- matrix(0.0, N_sim, K_sim)
for (i in seq_len(N_sim)) {
  theta_i <- as.vector(t(beta_sim) %*% X_sim_raw[i, ])
  mu_i    <- exp(theta_i - max(theta_i)); mu_i <- mu_i / sum(mu_i)
  rho_i   <- plogis(a_rho_sim * theta_i - tau_sim)
  phi_i   <- exp(sum(delta_sim * X_sim_raw[i, ]))
  z       <- rbinom(K_sim, 1L, rho_i)
  A       <- which(z == 1L)
  if (length(A) == 0L) next
  if (length(A) == 1L) { Y_sim_raw[i, A] <- 1.0; next }
  mu_A    <- mu_i[A] / sum(mu_i[A])
  Y_sim_raw[i, A] <- c(rdirichlet(1L, phi_i * mu_A))
}

# Drop all-zero rows; normalise to simplex
keep_s   <- rowSums(Y_sim_raw) > 0
Y_sim_r  <- Y_sim_raw[keep_s, ]
x_sim_r  <- x_sim_raw[keep_s]
X_sim_r  <- X_sim_raw[keep_s, ]
Y_sim_r  <- Y_sim_r / rowSums(Y_sim_r)
N_sim_r  <- nrow(Y_sim_r)

# Train / test split at x = 0.5
tr_s  <- x_sim_r <= 0.5
te_s  <- !tr_s
Y_tr  <- Y_sim_r[tr_s, ];  X_tr  <- X_sim_r[tr_s, ]
Y_te  <- Y_sim_r[te_s, ];  X_te  <- X_sim_r[te_s, ]
N_tr  <- sum(tr_s);          N_te  <- sum(te_s)

cat(sprintf("N_train = %d   N_test = %d\n", N_tr, N_te))

# How many test zero-patterns are unseen in training?
pats_tr <- apply(Y_tr > 0, 1, paste, collapse = ",")
pats_te <- apply(Y_te > 0, 1, paste, collapse = ",")
cat(sprintf("Unique train patterns: %d   Test patterns unseen in train: %d / %d\n",
            length(unique(pats_tr)),
            sum(!pats_te %in% unique(pats_tr)), N_te))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sim-dgp
#| fig-cap: "True inclusion probability ρ_k(x) for each simulated prey. The dashed line marks the train/test split at x = 0.5. Prey 1–2 dominate at low x; prey 4–5 dominate at high x."
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 7

x_seq    <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.005)
X_seq    <- cbind(1, x_seq)
prey_lbl <- paste0("prey_", seq_len(K_sim))

rho_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(K_sim), function(k) {
  theta_k <- as.vector(X_seq %*% beta_sim[, k])
  data.frame(x = x_seq, prey = prey_lbl[k],
             rho = plogis(a_rho_sim * theta_k - tau_sim))
}))

ggplot(rho_df, aes(x = x, y = rho, colour = prey)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.25, y = 0.97, label = "Train", size = 3.5, colour = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.75, y = 0.97, label = "Test",  size = 3.5, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(title = "True inclusion probability by covariate",
       x = "x", y = expression(rho[k](x)), colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: sim-fit
#| cache: true

sim_args4 <- list(chains = 4L, parallel_chains = 4L,
                  iter_warmup = 1000L, iter_sampling = 1000L,
                  seed = 42L, refresh = 0L)

y_tr_ls <- lapply(seq_len(N_tr), function(j) Y_tr[j, ])

# Ordered Dirichlet
fit_ord_s <- do.call(ord_mod$sample, c(
  list(data = list(N = N_tr, K = K_sim, P = P_sim, X = X_tr, y = y_tr_ls)),
  sim_args4))

# Coupled Ordered Dirichlet
fit_cpl_s <- do.call(coupled_mod$sample, c(
  list(data = list(N = N_tr, K = K_sim, P = P_sim,
                   X = X_tr, y = y_tr_ls, eps = 1e-10)),
  sim_args4))

# ZADR — log_theta from training patterns only
tr_counts_s <- table(pats_tr)
lth_tr_s    <- log(as.numeric(tr_counts_s[pats_tr]) / N_tr)

fit_zad_s <- do.call(zadr_mod$sample, c(
  list(data = list(N = N_tr, K = K_sim, P = P_sim,
                   X = X_tr, y = y_tr_ls, log_theta = lth_tr_s)),
  sim_args4))

cat("Rhat check (max across models):\n")
rhat_max <- max(
  max(fit_ord_s$summary()$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(fit_cpl_s$summary()$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(fit_zad_s$summary()$rhat, na.rm = TRUE)
)
cat(sprintf("  max Rhat = %.3f\n", rhat_max))
```

```{r}
#| label: sim-eval
#| cache: true

S_se <- 500L   # posterior draws to use for evaluation

d_ord_s <- fit_ord_s$draws(c("beta_raw", "tau", "delta"), format = "df") |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |> slice_sample(n = S_se)

d_cpl_s <- fit_cpl_s$draws(c("beta_raw", "tau", "a_rho", "delta"), format = "df") |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |> slice_sample(n = S_se)

d_zad_s <- fit_zad_s$draws(c("beta_raw", "phi"), format = "df") |>
  select(-starts_with(".")) |> slice_sample(n = S_se)

# ZADR log_theta for test observations (unseen patterns get log(1/N_tr))
lth_te_s <- ifelse(
  pats_te %in% names(tr_counts_s),
  log(as.numeric(tr_counts_s[pats_te]) / N_tr),
  log(1 / N_tr)
)

# Per-test-observation log predictive density
lpd_te <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(N_te), function(j) {
  y_j <- Y_te[j, ]; x_j <- X_te[j, ]

  lp_o <- vapply(seq_len(S_se), function(s) {
    b   <- extr_beta_K(d_ord_s[s, ], P_sim, K_sim)
    del <- as.numeric(d_ord_s[s, paste0("delta[", 1:P_sim, "]")])
    ord_lpdf_r(y_j, as.vector(t(b) %*% x_j), exp(sum(del * x_j)),
               as.numeric(d_ord_s$tau[s]))
  }, numeric(1L))

  lp_c <- vapply(seq_len(S_se), function(s) {
    b   <- extr_beta_K(d_cpl_s[s, ], P_sim, K_sim)
    del <- as.numeric(d_cpl_s[s, paste0("delta[", 1:P_sim, "]")])
    coupled_lpdf_r(y_j, as.vector(t(b) %*% x_j), exp(sum(del * x_j)),
                   as.numeric(d_cpl_s$tau[s]), as.numeric(d_cpl_s$a_rho[s]))
  }, numeric(1L))

  lp_z <- vapply(seq_len(S_se), function(s) {
    b  <- extr_beta_1(d_zad_s[s, ], P_sim, K_sim)
    mu <- exp(as.vector(t(b) %*% x_j)); mu <- mu / sum(mu)
    zadr_lpdf_r(y_j, mu, as.numeric(d_zad_s$phi[s]), lth_te_s[j])
  }, numeric(1L))

  data.frame(
    obs     = j,
    x_val   = x_j[2],
    seen    = pats_te[j] %in% names(tr_counts_s),
    model   = c("Ordered Dirichlet", "Coupled Ord. Dirichlet", "ZADR (fixed θ)"),
    lpd     = c(lse(lp_o) - log(S_se),
                lse(lp_c) - log(S_se),
                lse(lp_z) - log(S_se))
  )
}))
```

```{r}

lpd_te |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(ELPD = sum(lpd), SE = sd(lpd) * sqrt(N_te), .groups = "drop") |>
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sim-patterns
#| fig-cap: "Zero patterns seen in training (left) vs encountered in the test set (right). Each row is one unique pattern; cells are coloured if the component is active. Patterns shift from prey 1–2 dominating in training to prey 4–5 dominating in the test set."
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 9

pat_to_df <- function(pats, split_label) {
  upats <- unique(pats)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(upats, function(p) {
    bits <- as.integer(strsplit(p, ",")[[1]])
    data.frame(
      pattern = p,
      prey    = paste0("prey_", seq_len(K_sim)),
      active  = bits == 1,
      count   = sum(pats == p),
      split   = split_label
    )
  }))
}

pat_df <- rbind(pat_to_df(pats_tr, "Train (x ≤ 0.5)"),
                pat_to_df(pats_te, "Test (x > 0.5)"))

ggplot(pat_df, aes(x = prey, y = reorder(pattern, count), fill = active)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#1b7837", "FALSE" = "#f7f7f7"),
                    labels = c("TRUE" = "active", "FALSE" = "zero")) +
  facet_wrap(~split, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Active-prey patterns by split",
       x = NULL, y = "Pattern (sorted by frequency)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top")
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "LOO-IC comparison. Lower LOOIC = better out-of-sample predictive accuracy."

loo_tbl |>
  mutate(delta_looic = looic - min(looic)) |>
  arrange(looic) |>
  select(Model = model, Family = family, Covariates = covars,
         LOOIC = looic, SE = se, `ΔLOOIC` = delta_looic) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

**Model structure comparison**

| Feature | zoid | Ordered Dirichlet | Coupled Ord. Dirichlet | ZADR (fixed θ) | ZADR (Bayes θ) |
|---------|------|-------------------|------------------------|----------------|----------------|
| Zero mechanism | Per-category zero-inflation | Single shared threshold τ (conditioned on A_i ≠ ∅) | Independent Bernoulli per component; empty set = all-zero row | Empirical (θ_b = n_b/N) | Bayesian (θ ~ Dirichlet) |
| All-zero rows | No | No (conditioned away) | Yes (native) | Yes (via zero pattern) | Yes (via zero pattern) |
| Inclusion scale | — | Fixed (a_ρ = 1) | Estimated a_ρ > 0 | — | — |
| Mean direction | Softmax per-category intercepts | Softmax(β'X) | Softmax(β'X) | Softmax(β'X), renorm. to active | Softmax(β'X), renorm. to active |
| Precision | Fixed overdispersion φ | Log-linear φ_i = exp(δ'X_i) | Log-linear φ_i = exp(δ'X_i) | Single shared φ | Single shared φ |
| Parameters (intercept-only) | K − 1 + K overdispersion | (K − 1) + 1 (τ) + 1 (δ) | (K − 1) + 1 (τ) + 1 (a_ρ) + 1 (δ) | (K − 1) + 1 (φ) | (K − 1) + 1 (φ) + B − 1 (θ) |
| θ uncertainty | — | — | — | None (fixed at MLE) | Full posterior via Dirichlet prior |

The trade-off is flexibility vs parsimony: zoid fits independent zero rates per prey item; the ordered Dirichlet ties sparsity to a single global threshold τ; the coupled ordered Dirichlet relaxes both by adding an inclusion-scale $a_\rho$ and allowing all-zero rows; ZADR (fixed θ) estimates pattern probabilities as plug-in MLEs; ZADR (Bayes θ) propagates uncertainty in pattern probabilities through the posterior via a Dirichlet prior.
